notes: Slice is dominated by two clean, contiguous runs: GameSpy SDK (0x61af70-0x62317f, covering auth/query protocol, ghttp HTTP client, encTypeX RC4 cipher, socket helpers, master-server connect) and MSVC CRT/runtime (0x623142-0x6315a2, covering delay-load thunks, __unlock_file/__getptd file-handle internals, libm floating point support, mainCRTStartup 'entry', TLS teardown). The GameSpy<->CRT boundary at DelayLoad_ShellExecuteA (0x623142) is exact (prior function 0x623110 ends precisely there) and well supported by callee evidence on both sides. Spot-checked ~10 functions via pack.py across both runs (RC4 KSA/PRGA at 0x623020/0x623110/0x622f20/0x622f60/0x622f7c, SWAR strchr at 0x6257e0, master-server connect at 0x61ea20, auth query builder at 0x61af70) and all confirm their assigned module. Only one function contradicts its assigned module.

disputes.reason: Decompiled body builds the literal URL "http://hpcup.bungie.net/motd/vercheck.asp?productid=%d&versionuniqueid=%s&distid=%d" (a bungie.net-hosted endpoint, i.e. Halo PC's own message-of-the-day/update-version-check feature) and just forwards it to the neighboring ghttpGet-style call (FUN_0061bd80). This is Bungie/Halo-authored game logic that merely calls into the GameSpy ghttp library, not GameSpy SDK code itself -- unlike every other function in the surrounding run, none of which reference a bungie.net string. The original assigner flagged this with only 0.6 confidence, i.e. already uncertain. Proposed module is a best guess (Halo's own network/update-check code); 'main' or 'shell' are plausible alternatives if this project's convention places version-check UI elsewhere, but it should not stay lib:gamespy.
